articles.title: Link preview shows no image? 7 og:image checks for Slack, X, Discord and LinkedIn
articles.excerpt: Your page looks fine in the browser, but when you paste the URL into Slack, X, Discord or LinkedIn you get a title and maybe a description, with no image. The crawler usually isn't broken. It's almost…
articles.body: Your page looks fine in the browser, but when you paste the URL into Slack, X, Discord or LinkedIn you get a title and maybe a description, with no image . The crawler usually isn't broken. It's almost always one of these. 1. The tags only exist after JavaScript runs Link-preview crawlers read the raw HTML the server returns. Most don't execute JavaScript. If your og: tags are injected by React/Vue on the client (a plain SPA, or react-helmet without SSR), the crawler never sees them. Check what the crawler sees: curl -s https://yoursite.com/page | grep -i 'og:image' If that prints nothing, render the tags on the server (SSR/SSG, or your framework's metadata API). 2.

articles.title: AWS Glue Concurrent Execution: What Happens When Multiple Jobs Write to the Same S3 Location?
articles.excerpt: Imagine you have two AWS Glue jobs running in production. Both jobs are processing customer data. Both read different source datasets, perform transformations, and write their results to the same S3 l…
articles.body: Imagine you have two AWS Glue jobs running in production. Both jobs are processing customer data. Both read different source datasets, perform transformations, and write their results to the same S3 location. Everything works fine when you execute them individually. But one day, both jobs start running at almost the same time. One job finishes successfully. The other also reports success. However, when you query the final data using Athena, some records are missing, some records appear twice, and the output doesn't look the way you expected. Where did things go wrong? This is one of the important problems to understand when building production data pipelines with AWS Glue and Amazon S3.

articles.title: Hubble Telescope sees cosmic 'cat's tail' that could wrap around Earth and the sun 500 times
articles.excerpt: Using the Hubble Space Telescope, astronomers have investigated a cosmic cat's tail formed when two Pluto-sized bodies smashed together.
articles.body: Using the Hubble Space Telescope, astronomers have investigated a cosmic cat's tail, finding it likely formed after two Pluto-sized bodies smashed together. The feature, nicknamed the Cat's Tail, extends out from the debris disk known as Beta Pictoris which is located in a planetary system located 63 light-years away. This tail would put that of the average tabby to shame: It's so long that it could curl around the sun-Earth system about 500 times. That's about as long as 200 trillion house cats. The major difference between our solar system and the planetary system that hosts the Cat's Tail is the latter's relative youth. While our solar system is around 4.6 billion years old , Beta Pictoris is a cosmic kitten no more than a few million years old.

articles.title: UEFI bootkit infected fully patched Windows machines. Is Microsoft to blame?
articles.excerpt: UEFI bootkit BlackX exploits Microsoft's lack of clarity around Secure Boot protections.
articles.body: In 2023, malware tracked as BlackLotus became the first publicly documented in-the-wild UEFI bootkit capable of bypassing Secure Boot on fully updated Windows 11 systems. With the industry-wide chain-of-trust mechanism subverted, the malware was able to run malicious code before Windows was fully loaded and many security defenses were operational. Microsoft had already patched the vulnerability that BlackLotus exploited in 2022. In 2023 and 2024, Microsoft issued additional updates. The first added a new certificate that no longer trusted the vulnerable boot managers. The second provided the means to revoke trust in the digital certificate used to sign older vulnerable Windows boot managers.

articles.body: On Aug. 2, 2027, darkness will fall on Tatooine. The path of the " eclipse of the century" crosses southern Tunisia, putting several of the most famous Star Wars filming locations in the moon's shadow for up to four minutes. Around Tozeur, eclipse chasers can experience totality among the dunes of Mos Espa and the rocky Jundland Wastes, while on Djerba, locations used for Mos Eisley and Obi-Wan Kenobi's home will also briefly go dark. Other iconic sites are tantalizingly close to — but beyond — the southern edge of the path of totality. For example, Hotel Sidi Idriss , used as Lars Homestead in the original movie and in Attack of the Clones , gets only a 99.98% partial eclipse.

articles.excerpt: You're going to need a lot of extra storage space on your console if you're planning to play Grand Theft Auto VI later this month. Rockstar Games confirmed on Tuesday that the preload file will requir…
articles.body: You're going to need a lot of extra storage space on your console if you're planning to play Grand Theft Auto VI later this month. Rockstar Games confirmed on Tuesday that the preload file will require up to 212GB "depending on your device." Rockstar says you can start preloading the game on the PlayStation 5 on Tuesday, November 10th at 12AM in your local time zone, while users on Xbox Series X / S devices can start preloading on November 10th at 12AM GMT. The company says to "make sure you've got ample space to begin pre-loading as soon as possible." Rockstar also posted a support page with more information about preloading the game. … Read the full story at The Verge.

articles.title: OpenAI seems to be silently re-enabling model training on Codex chats
articles.excerpt: My company is pretty paranoid about leaking IP to the frontier labs through prompts, so we've all been diligent about disabling data sharing in Codex/Claude Code/etc. But yesterday my coworkers and I…
articles.body: My company is pretty paranoid about leaking IP to the frontier labs through prompts, so we've all been diligent about disabling data sharing in Codex/Claude Code/etc. But yesterday my coworkers and I noticed that the setting had been silently reenabled in Codex. None of us knowingly opted back in. You can check your settings here: https://chatgpt.com/settings/data-controls. Look for "Improve the model for everyone". Curious if this is an isolated issue or something more widespread. EDIT: looks like this has been noted before https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49643556 EDIT: apparently you can also turn off data sharing here: https://privacy.openai.com/policies?modal=take-control
